compareCandidate.label: Proportion vs. ratio
compareCandidate.description: A ratio is one comparison (3:5). A proportion is the equality of two ratios (3:5 = 6:10). Proportions let you find a missing value by keeping the ratio constant.

processes: Solving for an unknown using cross products
plainLanguageExplanation: A proportion is a statement that two ratios are equal. 3:5 = 6:10 says the mix of 3 to 5 is the same as 6 to 10 — just doubled. Proportions are the tool for scaling: if a recipe that feeds 4 needs 2 cups of flour, feeding 8 needs 4 cups — the ratio of people to flour stays the same. To solve a proportion with a missing value, use cross products: in a/b = c/d, multiply a × d and b × c — they must be equal. So in 3/5 = x/10, cross multiply 3 × 10 = 5 × x, giving 30 = 5x and x = 6. Proportions power unit conversion, map reading, and scaling recipes.

whyItMatters: Proportions solve real scaling problems — doubling recipes, converting units, reading maps, and comparing rates. They are also the foundation of direct variation and linear functions in algebra, so mastering them now pays off for years.
didYouKnow: Photocopiers use proportions — 'enlarge 150%' scales every dimension of a drawing by the same ratio, which is exactly a proportion applied to a whole shape.
compareReason: A proportion is just an equal-ratio statement — comparing the single ratio with its equality makes the jump to solving clear.
